notes: Interaction-level analysis built on the verified profile. Local arithmetic/accounting findings (LOCAL-001..006) are NOT re-derived; this scan resolves the profile's deferred cross-contract questions and cross-references ledger M-01/M-02/C-02.

findings.title: Cross-contract reentrancy in claim/withdraw/stake: reward debt settled AFTER token mint/transfer; exploitable only if phUSD.mint or rewardToken.transfer yields control to the recipient
findings.buildsOn: LOCAL-002 (guard gap + claim-before-settle ordering verified locally; exploitability deferred to Tier 2)
findings.description: claim() (L374-381), withdraw() (L334-369) and stake() (L295-328) call _claimRewards() which performs external calls phUSD.mint(user,..) (L442) and rewardToken.safeTransfer(user,..) (L448) BEFORE the caller writes back user.phUSDDebt/user.stableDebt. None of these three functions carry nonReentrant (only collectReward does). _updatePool() sets lastRewardTime=block.timestamp on the outer call, so a same-block re-entry skips re-accrual (L390 early return) but recomputes the SAME pending amount against the still-stale debt, minting/transferring it again on each re-entry.
findings.precondition: Either (a) phUSD.mint(recipient,..) invokes a callback into recipient, or (b) rewardToken.safeTransfer(recipient,..) invokes a recipient hook (ERC777-style / non-standard token). The recipient must be attacker-controlled (trivial: stake to your own contract, or claim from it). Profile trust assumptions and the IFlax interface (plain mint(address,uint256), no hook) and the standard-stable assumption for rewardToken mean NEITHER in-scope token hands back control today; no ERC777/hook token exists in the project's own source (only unused in the OZ lib).
attackSequence: Attacker contract has a non-zero staked position with accrued pending rewards.
Attacker calls claim() (or withdraw/stake).
_updatePool() runs; _claimRewards() computes pending = amount*accX/PRECISION - debt and calls phUSD.mint(attacker, pending) [and/or rewardToken.safeTransfer].
IF that token hands control to the attacker, the attacker re-enters claim() before debts are updated.
Re-entry recomputes the SAME pending (debt still stale) and mints/transfers again; repeat until gas/hook depth exhausted.
Outer frames then finally write debt once -- but N payouts already happened.
findings.impact: If a hooked token is ever wired: (1) unbounded phUSD inflation (phUSD is minted, not balance-backed -> direct supply inflation, breaks INV-2 at the protocol level), and (2) drain of the contract's entire rewardToken balance (all other stakers' unclaimed stable + rewardBalance), breaking INV-3. Under the stated standard-ERC20 / non-reentrant-mint assumptions it is NOT triggerable.
findings.attackVector: Token-callback-driven re-entry into claim/withdraw/stake while reward debt is stale, yielding N-claim of the same pending amount.
findings.c4Reasoning: Realistically Low/QA (defense-in-depth CEI violation) because both in-scope tokens are hook-free by design and the assumption matches repo known-invalid policy (weird/callback ERC20 out of scope except USDT). BUT phUSD is the protocol's OWN mintable token held under mint authority by this contract; the day a transfer/mint hook is added anywhere on the phUSD or reward path, this becomes Plausible High (direct inflation + reward drain). Surfaced for recall (Law 1) with an explicit cheap fix.
findings.recommendation: Add nonReentrant to stake/withdraw/claim, OR reorder _claimRewards/callers so user.phUSDDebt/user.stableDebt are written BEFORE the external mint/transfer (full CEI). The fix is one modifier or a 3-line reorder and removes the conditional-High entirely.

findings.title: pauseWithdraw mutates user.amount without rebasing reward debt -> subsequent claim/withdraw/stake underflow-reverts, bricking the account's normal operations (principal recoverable only by re-pausing)
findings.buildsOn: Ledger M-01 (tier-3 verified counterexample). This entry verifies the exact path and adds the principal-recoverability nuance.
findings.description: pauseWithdraw (L245-261) decrements user.amount (L251) and totalStaked (L254) and transfers principal, but does NOT call _updatePool, does NOT reset user.phUSDDebt/user.stableDebt, and does NOT enforce MINIMUM_STAKE. This violates the premise behind profile INV-5 ('debt reset on every amount change') -- pauseWithdraw is precisely the path that changes amount WITHOUT resetting debt. After a PARTIAL pauseWithdraw, debt is still sized for the pre-withdraw (larger) amount, so the next _claimRewards subtraction (userDetails.amount*accX/PRECISION - debt, L440/L446) underflows and reverts under 0.8.19 checked arithmetic.
findings.precondition: User has a position with debt anchored at amount=S (i.e. phUSDDebt = S*accX_at_anchor/PRECISION). Contract gets paused. User calls pauseWithdraw(w) with 0 < w < S (a PARTIAL emergency exit). Underflow on next claim occurs whenever (S-w)*accX_now < S*accX_anchor, i.e. whenever the accumulator has not grown by at least a factor S/(S-w) since the debt anchor -- which is the common case (e.g. withdraw 50% needs >2x accumulator growth to AVOID the revert; with phUSDPerSecond/accStable flat or modest growth it always underflows).
attackSequence: User stakes S; debt anchored (phUSDDebt=S*accPhUSD/PRECISION, stableDebt=S*accStable/PRECISION).
Pauser pauses the contract.
User uses the emergency exit partially: pauseWithdraw(w), 0<w<S. Now user.amount=S-w but debts unchanged.
Pauser unpauses.
User calls claim() (or withdraw / stake): _updatePool() then _claimRewards() computes (S-w)*accX/PRECISION - (S*accX_anchor/PRECISION) -> underflow -> revert.
findings.impact: Account-level brick: while UNPAUSED, claim() reverts, withdraw() reverts (it calls _claimRewards first, L341), and stake() reverts (calls _claimRewards when amount>0, L308-310). All pending rewards for that account are unrecoverable. Principal (the remaining S-w) is NOT permanently lost: pauseWithdraw does not touch debt, so the user CAN recover principal -- but ONLY while the contract is paused (whenPaused). If the pauser never pauses again (or pauser==address(0), see CODE-004), the remaining principal is stranded indefinitely. Not attacker-forceable on a third party (pauseWithdraw is msg.sender-only) -> self-inflicted footgun via the emergency exit, with no warning.
findings.codeSnippet:
user.amount -= amount;        // L251  amount changes...
totalStaked -= amount;        // L254
IERC20(address(phUSD)).safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount);  // ...but phUSDDebt/stableDebt NEVER rebased
// later, _claimRewards: (userDetails.amount * accPhUSDPerShare)/PRECISION - userDetails.phUSDDebt  // underflow
findings.attackVector: Sequence pauseWithdraw(partial) -> unpause -> claim/withdraw/stake triggers checked-arithmetic underflow in _claimRewards.
findings.c4Reasoning: Medium: no direct theft and principal is recoverable via a re-pause, but the protocol's core functions (claim/withdraw/stake) are bricked for the affected account and accrued rewards are lost -- a function/availability impact with a value leak, matching C4 Medium and the existing ledger M-01 classification.
findings.recommendation: In pauseWithdraw, either call _updatePool()+_claimRewards() (or at minimum rebase user.phUSDDebt/user.stableDebt to user.amount*accX/PRECISION) after adjusting amount, and apply the same dust/MINIMUM_STAKE rule as withdraw.

findings.title: Permissionless collectReward lets any non-staker re-anchor rewardPerSecond and force pool updates at dust cost, manipulating realized stable-distribution velocity to stakers
findings.buildsOn: Ledger M-02 (code-analysis only) + LOCAL-001 (per-update rate re-anchor = exponential decay).
findings.description: collectReward (L270-286) is permissionless (only require: amount>0). It runs _updatePool() (which under LOCAL-001 distributes accrued stable then re-anchors rewardPerSecond=rewardBalance*PRECISION/depletionDuration, L416), then adds the caller's amount and re-anchors again (L283). Because the rate is recomputed remaining/duration on EVERY update, forcing frequent updates pushes the system from the near-linear single-chunk regime toward continuous exponential decay (dB/dt=-B/D), lengthening the tail. An external party with no stake can drive this by calling collectReward repeatedly with as little as 1 wei.
findings.precondition: An active pool with stakers and a non-zero rewardBalance. Attacker needs only gas + dust amounts of rewardToken and approval. No stake, no role, no privilege required. Most effective in a quiet pool where natural stake/withdraw/claim interactions are infrequent (so the attacker, not organic usage, controls update cadence).
attackSequence: Yield-accumulator funds a chunk R; rewardPerSecond=R/depletionDuration.
Griefer repeatedly calls collectReward(1 wei) (or just enough to pass amount>0).
Each call forces _updatePool -> distributes the tiny slice accrued so far, then re-anchors rate to remaining/duration (LOCAL-001).
High update frequency keeps the system in the slow exponential-decay regime, so stakers receive their stable rewards more slowly than the intended 'distribute rewardBalance over depletionDuration'.
Cost to griefer = gas + negligible dust (the dust is additive to rewardBalance, so the attacker even slightly subsidizes the pool while degrading its timing).
findings.impact: Griefing / denial of yield velocity: an unprivileged external party gains fine-grained control over the realized rate at which stable rewards reach stakers, and can indefinitely stretch the depletion tail. No theft and no direct loss of principal; the harm is to protocol function (timely reward distribution) and to staker experience. Magnitude is bounded/economic and partially overlaps the LOCAL-001 documented V1 behavior; the NEW element here is that the lever is open to anyone (access control), not just organic participants.
findings.attackVector: Spam permissionless collectReward to control _updatePool cadence and re-anchor the depletion rate, slowing stable distribution to existing stakers.
findings.c4Reasoning: Medium: protocol function/availability (reward-distribution timing) is degradable by an unprivileged actor at trivial cost, with stated external assumptions (the LOCAL-001 recompute), and no direct asset loss -- matching C4 Medium and the existing ledger M-02. NOTE: the economic-velocity dimension overlaps econ-scanner's mandate; reported here from the access-control (permissionless entry point) angle.
findings.recommendation: Restrict collectReward to the trusted yield-accumulator (or an allow-list), and/or decouple the depletion-rate anchor from per-update recompute (the PhlimboV2 approach) so funding/update cadence cannot reshape the distribution curve.

findings.title: setPauser(0) + emergencyTransfer sequence permanently bricks ALL withdrawals: contract is force-paused with no valid unpauser and the pauseWithdraw escape hatch is drained dead, while userInfo/totalStaked stay non-zero
findings.buildsOn: LOCAL-006 (permanent-pause footgun) + ledger C-02 (accounting not zeroed). This entry establishes the full cross-function permanent-brick-of-withdrawals sequence.
findings.description: Three independently reasonable owner/role facts compose into an unrecoverable state: (1) setPauser(address(0)) is explicitly documented (L204, IPhlimbo) as the way to 'disable pausing'; (2) emergencyTransfer (L214-227) calls _pause() UNCONDITIONALLY (L226) after sweeping the entire phUSD and rewardToken balances; (3) unpause() requires msg.sender==pauser (L198). With pauser==address(0), no caller can ever satisfy unpause(), so _pause() is permanent. stake/withdraw/claim are whenNotPaused -> all revert forever. The only whenPaused escape, pauseWithdraw, calls phUSD.safeTransfer (L257) but the contract's phUSD balance was just drained to 0 by emergencyTransfer -> reverts. userInfo and totalStaked are never zeroed, so on-chain accounting still claims users hold stakes that no function can return.
findings.precondition: Owner has (legitimately, per the docstring) set pauser=address(0) to disable the pauser role. Owner later invokes emergencyTransfer (an intended nuclear escape hatch) -- e.g. to move funds to safety during an incident, intending to redistribute or redeploy. No malice required.
attackSequence: Owner calls setPauser(address(0)) -- documented as 'disable pausing'.
Incident occurs; owner calls emergencyTransfer(safe) to rescue funds.
emergencyTransfer drains all phUSD + rewardToken, then _pause().
Contract is now paused permanently (unpause needs pauser==0, impossible).
Users try pauseWithdraw -> reverts (no phUSD left to transfer).
Users try stake/withdraw/claim -> revert (whenNotPaused).
Result: every staker's recorded principal is permanently unwithdrawable and the contract can never be reopened.
findings.impact: Permanent brick of ALL user withdrawal paths and loss of access to all staked principal, reached via a sequence of individually-sensible owner actions. This is the non-obvious composition (setPauser(0) docstring suggests it is safe; the auto-pause in emergencyTransfer and the dead escape hatch are the surprises) -- a Law-3 footgun, NOT obvious misuse, hence in scope.
findings.attackVector: Non-malicious owner sequence (setPauser(0) then emergencyTransfer) yields an unrecoverable paused+drained state with non-zeroed accounting.
findings.c4Reasoning: Low / Centralization rather than High: it requires owner actions and the owner is trusted for KNOWING acts. The fund-sweep itself is an obvious owner power (suppressed). What is NON-obvious -- and therefore reportable as an operational hazard -- is that the documented 'disable pausing' setting turns emergencyTransfer's auto-pause into a PERMANENT lock that also kills the pauseWithdraw escape and leaves accounting non-zeroed. Aligns with ledger C-02 + LOCAL-006.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) let owner unpause (e.g. unpause callable by owner OR pauser), or (b) make emergencyTransfer zero out userInfo/totalStaked when it sweeps principal, and/or (c) do not auto-_pause() when pauser==address(0). Document the setPauser(0) <-> emergencyTransfer interaction prominently.

findings.title: pauseWithdraw can drive totalStaked to dust (no MINIMUM_STAKE), amplifying accStablePerShare per-update growth and risking precision blow-up / _updatePool overflow-DoS once unpaused
findings.description: Because pauseWithdraw (L245-261) does not enforce MINIMUM_STAKE (LOCAL-005), the set of stakers can pauseWithdraw their positions down to near-1-wei residuals, so after unpause totalStaked can be a tiny number. _updatePool then computes accStablePerShare += toDistribute*PRECISION/totalStaked (L410) and accPhUSDPerShare += phUSDReward*PRECISION/totalStaked (L422) with a very small divisor, making the accumulators grow extremely fast. The downstream products amount*accX (L440/L446) then risk approaching 2^256 over time -> checked-arithmetic revert in _updatePool, which would DoS the whole pool (every stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward calls _updatePool).
findings.precondition: Contract paused; multiple stakers pauseWithdraw down to dust residuals (or a single staker dusts and others fully exit), leaving totalStaked at a tiny value; contract then unpaused and rewards continue to flow / time passes across many updates. Requires extreme/contrived magnitudes -- the profile notes products stay within bounds for REALISTIC token magnitudes, so this is a tail risk, not a demonstrated revert.
attackSequence: Pauser pauses.
Stakers use pauseWithdraw to leave sub-MINIMUM_STAKE dust positions (allowed -- no dust rule).
Pauser unpauses; totalStaked is now tiny.
Over many _updatePool calls with a tiny divisor, accStablePerShare/accPhUSDPerShare inflate toward overflow; eventually amount*accX overflows and _updatePool reverts, DoSing all pool interactions.
findings.impact: Potential pool-wide DoS (all interactions revert) via accumulator overflow once totalStaked is dusted. Also re-weakens the MINIMUM_STAKE / per-share precision guard the constant exists to provide. No theft. Realistically requires contrived magnitudes; reported for recall (Law 1) at low confidence.
findings.codeSnippet:
accStablePerShare += (toDistribute * PRECISION) / totalStaked;   // L410 tiny totalStaked -> huge increments
accPhUSDPerShare  += (phUSDReward * PRECISION) / totalStaked;     // L422
findings.attackVector: Dust-out totalStaked via pauseWithdraw, then let accumulators inflate until _updatePool products overflow.
findings.c4Reasoning: Low / QA: depends on contrived magnitudes and the profile's overflow-within-bounds note for realistic tokens; the concrete, higher-confidence harm of the same root cause is the MINIMUM_STAKE invariant weakening (LOCAL-005). Surfaced as a low-confidence interaction tail risk rather than a standalone High.
findings.recommendation: Apply the withdraw dust-forces-full-exit rule inside pauseWithdraw (and/or re-validate minimums on unpause) so totalStaked cannot be left at dust.
